open_points.subject: Client Portal offline projection
open_points.text: “no other service keeps a customer record or a copy of its values, except as fixed in a document it issued” conflicts with “Portal serves the last projection it was permitted to keep locally” and with `context` containing display name and address
open_points.question: May Client Portal persist an offline copy of Registry-held personal values, and if so, which fields and under what exception to R0-80?
options: Permit the offline projection as an explicit exception
Permit only non-personal fields in the offline projection
Forbid the persisted offline projection
open_points.default_guess: Permit an offline projection containing only fields explicitly authorized for Portal, and state it as an exception to the no-copy rule

open_points.subject: PresuPro billing-data read
open_points.text: “Name, phone, e-mail and language are all the customer's contact data” and “contact data still reaches the owner alone” conflict with the billing action returning “name, kind, tax id, legal name” to PresuPro
open_points.question: May PresuPro receive the Customer's ordinary `name`, or must its billing-data output contain only fiscal fields such as legal name and tax id?
options: Return ordinary name to PresuPro and narrow the owner-only rule
Return only kind, tax id and legal name
Return ordinary name only when it is also the legal name
open_points.default_guess: Return only kind, tax id and legal name to PresuPro

open_points.subject: Customer erasure and fiscal data
open_points.text: “name, phone, e-mail and language are gone” leaves tax id and legal name unspecified, while R0-67 says the erased Customer “keeps its identity and the fact that it was erased” and R0-80 makes fiscal data part of the Customer's living personal data
open_points.question: When customer data is erased, are tax id and legal name erased too, or do they remain on the record?
options: Erase contact and fiscal data, leaving only identity and erased status
Erase only contact data and retain fiscal data
Provide separate contact-data and full-personal-data erasures
open_points.default_guess: Erase contact and fiscal data, leaving only identity and erased status

open_points.subject: Correction of customer fiscal data
open_points.text: The Customer stores optional “tax id (NIF/NIE/CIF) and legal name”, but “correct a customer” promises only “the Customer with the new contact data”
open_points.question: Which action lets the owner add, change or clear a Customer's tax id and legal name after recording it?
options: Extend `correct a customer` to fiscal data
Add a separate fiscal-data correction action
Make fiscal data immutable after creation
open_points.default_guess: Extend `correct a customer` to add, change or clear fiscal data

open_points.subject: Entity revision coverage
open_points.text: R0-35 says “A project, a customer and an object carry a revision that every accepted change moves” and “A change states the revision it was made against”, but stale-revision failures and next revisions are stated only for project and customer correction, not for archiving, adding a room, erasing, restricting, ending a relationship or other mutations
open_points.question: Exactly which actions must supply an expected revision, which entity's revision do they move, and do successful idempotent no-ops move it?
options: Every mutation of a project or customer requires and moves its revision
Only direct correction actions use revisions
Define revision participation separately for each action
open_points.default_guess: Require the current entity revision for every mutation of that entity, move it only when state changes, and leave it unchanged for idempotent no-ops

open_points.subject: Agent-session access version
open_points.text: “read the session's access” returns “the access version”, but no text says which grants, revocations, active-project changes, requests, answers or registration events move it, or whether writes must present it
open_points.question: What is the observable meaning of the access version, when does it change, and does it provide stale-write protection for owner and Kernel actions?
options: It changes on every access-state mutation and is required for writes
It changes on mutations but is informational only
Remove it because no behavior depends on it
open_points.default_guess: Change it on every mutation of the session's grants, active project or pending request and require it for owner changes that could race

open_points.subject: Legacy VPS Registry migration source
open_points.text: “Test instances — any other instance ... holds ... no production personal data” conflicts with importing customers, objects and projects from “the Registry on the VPS”; that legacy instance is not otherwise named as an actor or trust boundary
open_points.question: What is the status and trust boundary of the legacy VPS Registry while it holds the personal data used by the migration?
options: Define it as a temporary trusted legacy production source
Treat it as a test instance and remove production personal data before migration
Define a separate migration-source category with explicit access and retirement guarantees
open_points.default_guess: Define the VPS Registry as a temporary trusted legacy production source until the one-time migration and retirement complete

open_points.subject: Customer relationship end date
open_points.text: “The Customer marked as ended on that date” does not say whether the date is supplied by the owner or generated when Registry accepts the action
open_points.question: Is the relationship-end date the operation date or an owner-supplied effective date, and what dates are valid?
options: Use Registry's acceptance date
Accept an owner-supplied effective date
Store both recorded-at and effective dates
open_points.default_guess: Accept an owner-supplied effective date and separately retain the action timestamp in the audit log

open_points.subject: Anonymised project retained identifiers
open_points.text: R0-71 says an anonymised project “holds no personal value”, while it retains its id and artifact pointers; R0-26 says “a project's id is not anonymous by itself”, and R0-68 admits pointer values may contain personal information without being inspected or refused
open_points.question: What must be established or changed before a project retaining its id and artifact pointers may be reported as anonymised with no personal value?
options: Require an external non-reidentification check covering the id and every retained pointer
Remove or rewrite identifying pointers during anonymisation
Call the result redacted rather than anonymised and retain its personal-data classification
open_points.default_guess: Require a recorded non-reidentification determination covering the retained id and every pointer before allowing anonymisation
